summary: doctor's auth/env_vars/credentials_location checks must consult BOTH signals independently: a usable persisted oauth-token.json bundle (via pelotonPersistedBundleStatus) and bootstrapEnvSet (PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PASSWORD both set), not just cfg.AuthHeader()/cfg.CredentialSource, which only ever reflect config-file-derived fields. Any future regen must keep authConfigured's switch covering all three: header != "", bundleUsable, and bootstrapEnvSet -- dropping any one reintroduces a state where "Auth" and "Env Vars" contradict each other (e.g. a fresh install with valid env vars but no bundle file yet previously still reported "not configured").
reason: cfg.AuthHeader() is checked on the config loaded before any clientHook runs, so it is always empty for Peloton (the managed auth mints its bearer/session material into a separate on-disk bundle, never into the config's AuthHeaderVal/AccessToken fields at load time). Doctor was reporting "Auth: not configured", "ERROR missing required", and "credentials_location: none" simultaneously with "API: reachable" and successful authenticated calls -- a direct contradiction that cost hours of user time chasing a nonexistent external OAuth provisioning service. An adversarial self-review of the first pass caught a second instance of the same contradiction class for the opposite input (bootstrap env vars set, no bundle yet -- e.g. right after upgrading to this fix) and a third: the credentials-validation probe itself was still gated on cfg.AuthHeader() alone, so it silently skipped for a bundle-only user instead of running. Also swept the 'private OAuth wrapper' / 'managed OAuth bundle' / 'OAuth2 with refresh-token rotation' wording across auth.go, peloton_oauth.go, doctor.go, helpers.go, agent_context.go, mcp/tools.go, client.go's peloton-specific hint string, .printing-press.json's auth_env_var_specs/novel_features (source of the public registry.json catalog entry after the next regen), manifest.json's user_config descriptions (what Claude Desktop's Extensions settings UI shows), and SKILL.md/README.md's Auth Setup sections. Peloton has no OAuth wrapper or provisioning service; the CLI just needs PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PELOTON_OAUTH_PASSWORD set once.
validated_outcome: Tests TestDoctorReportsPersistedTokenWithoutBootstrapEnvVars, TestDoctorReportsNoCredentialsAnywhere, and TestDoctorReportsFreshBootstrapEnvVarsBeforeFirstLogin drive the real `doctor --json` command end-to-end (real cliutil.SetHomeOverride, a local httptest server for the reachability/credential probes, no live network) and assert all three states are distinguished correctly. Verified live against a real account: doctor now reports "credentials": "valid" (previously silently skipped) alongside the correct auth/env_vars state. Full go build/vet/test suite passes.
